good.text: I put a statue in my bedroom. Now two of us in there have good taste.
My bedroom shares a wall with the still. It bubbles me to sleep every night.
The miners carved my room from one perfect vein of blue stone. I sleep inside a gem.
My bedroom is so far from the trade depot that no elf will ever find it. Bliss.

bad.text: My bedroom shares a wall with the smelter. I sleep in a sauna.
They dug my bedroom right under the cistern. The ceiling drips with menace.
Someone stored three barrels of rotting meat in my room 'temporarily'. That was a season ago.
My bed is wooden. Every time the elves visit, I feel a tree judging me.

good.text: The overseer gave me a work order and every material was already in the stockpile. I nearly fainted.
I built a whole bridge today. It has not collapsed yet. Bridges are mostly about the 'yet'.
My workshop is twelve steps from the stockpile. I counted them, lovingly.
I made something so fine the broker begged to sell it. I said no. He wept.

bad.text: Somebody linked my lever to the wrong door. I have been flooding the barracks all morning.
I spent all day building a wall, and then another dwarf was told to take it down.
My job was suspended because a dwarf was standing in the way. Standing. For an hour.
I was drafted into the militia mid-project. My half-carved statue now looks like a potato.

good.text: I watched the water wheel turn all afternoon. It never once let me down.
A whole day with no orders. I polished my pick until I could see my beard in it.
Nothing to do, so I took the long way to the dining hall. All forty stairs. Bliss.
I sat in the statue garden and thought about nothing. The nothing was excellent.

bad.text: I have read the same wall engraving so many times I could carve it blindfolded.
I have been 'No Job' for so long it is practically my profession.
I paced the corridor until the floor was smooth. The engraver got the credit.
I asked the overseer for work. He assigned me to wait. I am terrible at waiting.

good.text: My new friend and I sat on the same bench without a word for an hour. Perfect friendship.
Three dwarves invited me to dinner. Two of them even knew my name.
I made a friend in the latest migrant wave. He hates trees too.
I have so many friends now I need a bigger table. A good problem.

bad.text: My only friend got married and now talks about nothing but their spouse's beard.
Everyone I know moved to a fortress across the mountains. They took the good mugs.
I sat in the tavern a whole evening. The tavern keeper was the only one who spoke, to charge me.
My best friend joined the militia. Now they march past me twice a day, eyes front.

good.text: I finally got to wander about aimlessly, as I require. My aimlessness was magnificent.
I needed to make something with my own hands. I made a ring. It is crooked. I love it.
I got some fighting practice in. Hitting a training dummy does wonders for the soul.
I learned something today. My brain had been begging for it like a hungry cat.

bad.text: I need to craft something, but every workshop is full of apprentices making mugs.
I have not been to a party in ages. I am not sure this fortress has ever had a party.
I need to see my family. They are three mountains and two goblin camps away.
I used to admire nature. Then I moved under a mountain. Poor planning on my part.

good.text: Something in the cave water made my beard grow an inch overnight. I am keeping it.
I breathed in some spores and now everything smells of fresh bread. Even the refuse pile.
A creature spat on me and now I cannot feel pain. I walked into a door twice, for science.
I feel fast. Faster than a hauler with an empty wheelbarrow. Faster than gossip.

bad.text: I touched a forgotten beast's blood and my fingers have been tingling for a week.
A cave spider bit me. My legs will not move, but my opinions are fully mobile.
I have sneezed sparks ever since I licked that crystal. The carpenters have banned me.
I keep forgetting my own name. The doctor blames the cavern dust. I say who is asking.

good.text: I can tell granite from diorite by licking it now. Progress has a taste.
The fort's legendary craftsdwarf nodded at me. Second-best day of my life, after my first ale.
I used to ruin one in three. Now I ruin one in ten. Basically a master.
I have become so good the workshop practically runs on my name. Well, on me.

bad.text: An apprentice half my age just out-skilled me. I am considering a strange mood out of spite.
I trained so long in the barracks I forgot how to do my actual job.
My work is stuck at well-crafted. The little dashes around it are laughing at me.
My teacher left before finishing my training. I now know exactly half a trade.

good.text: The smell from the butcher's shop is so strong it cured my three-year cold.
Somebody finally hauled the old goblin away. You could hear the whole fortress inhale.
I have learned to breathe through my beard. It filters out most of the purple.
Thanks to the smell, I have the whole corridor to myself. Nobody else will walk it.

bad.text: The refuse pile has grown so tall it has its own weather now.
There is a dead cat in the well room. The other cats know. The other cats are staring.
My mug tasted of rot this morning. The mug was clean. The air was not.
I sat down to dinner, but the smell had taken the seat first.

good.text: The fallen got a masterwork coffin. I have put my name down for the next one.
Our fallen hero got a memorial engraving. In it he is twice his real height. He earned it.
I outlived the forgotten beast. I plan to outlive everything else, too.
The goblin who stole my sock is dead. The sock is avenged.

bad.text: We buried my friend in a corridor because nobody had dug the tomb yet.
This time the coffin maker is the one who died. Nobody knows who makes his coffin.
Someone used my bedroom as a temporary morgue. Temporary, they said.
Three funerals this week. I have run out of solemn faces.

good.text: The rain filled every bucket in the fort. Nobody had to visit the carp well today.
The rain made the wildflowers smell nice. I said that out loud. I take it back.
I stood under the drawbridge and listened to the rain drum on it. Very soothing.
Rain means the elves stay home. I danced. Briefly.

bad.text: It rained into the trade depot. The cloth is soggy and the elves blamed me personally.
The rain flooded the entrance ramp. I slid down it on my back like an otter.
A rain cloud followed me from the woodpile to the door. I swear it was aiming.
The rain fell sideways today. Sideways! Not even the weather follows the plan.

good.text: I saw a bird today. It did not attack me. We parted as equals.
The stars came out and I counted eleven before going back in. Eleven is plenty.
Sunrise looks like magma rising. I finally see why surface folk put up with it.
I lay on the grass and the grass did not swallow me. Two stars out of five.

bad.text: A cloud covered the sun, then the sun came back. The sky cannot make up its mind.
I looked up and there was no ceiling. I looked down and there was a goblin.
The wind took my hat. The sky is a thief.
A bird dropped something on my beard. The sky has declared war.

good.text: Tried the new batch of sunshine. They named it after the sky, the only nice thing the sky ever did.
Somebody stacked a pyramid of full barrels in the stockpile. I stood and admired it for an hour.
Dwarven rum on a cold night. My toes, my beard and my outlook all warmed up.
The tavern keeper had my mug poured before I asked. That is love, in dwarf terms.

bad.text: Someone used my mug to mix paint. My ale now tastes faintly of blue.
The barrels went to the trade depot. The ale went with them. I went into despair.
Swamp whiskey again. It tastes exactly like its name.
I was slow to the barrel, and now a queue of thirsty miners stands between me and happiness.

good.text: The cook topped the roast with prickle berries. I stood up and saluted it.
Quarry bush leaf rolls. Crunchy, bitter, and exactly as dwarven as I am.
The cook named a dish after me. It is mostly pig tail, but it is mine.
Fresh cheese from our own goats. The cheese maker is my new favorite dwarf.

bad.text: Dinner was a single raw sweet pod, and I had to share it.
The roast was cooked over magma. Burnt outside, raw inside, middle still on fire.
The food stockpile was full of gnawed scraps and one very guilty-looking rat.
Someone took my meal off the table while I fetched ale. I suspect the dog.

good.text: The dining hall has a waterfall now. My ale has never felt so scenic.
They put a masterwork table in the dining hall. I ate gently, out of respect.
The dining hall opens onto the tavern now. Two steps from stew to song.
The new dining hall has so many seats I tried six before choosing one.

bad.text: The dining hall doubles as the hospital now. I ate my soup beside a dwarf getting stitches.
Forty dwarves and one table. We eat in shifts, like a mine.
The dining hall floor is sticky. Nobody will say with what.
They put the dining hall on the surface. The sky watches me eat.

good.text: I napped in the hay with the yaks. Best rest since the mountainhomes.
I slept through an entire goblin siege. I am told we won. Well rested and victorious.
My new bed is so soft I sank into it like a pick into clay.
I woke before the bell for once and watched the miners stagger in. Smug and refreshed.

bad.text: I fell asleep at my workshop and woke up with a chisel stuck to my cheek.
Nightmares again. I dreamt the elves had planted a tree in my bedroom.
My bed was taken, so I slept on the stairs. The stairs had other plans.
I was so tired I fell asleep walking and woke up in the caverns.

good.text: {deity} sent me a sign: a perfectly round pebble. I keep it in my sock.
The new temple has room to kneel and a little shelf for ale offerings. {deity} approves.
I asked {deity} for patience and was immediately assigned hauling. A test. I passed.
I prayed to {deity} at the new altar and felt the stone hum. Or a miner was digging below.

bad.text: The temple was turned into a stockpile. {deity} is now somewhere behind the stone bins.
A dwarf who follows a different god prays in my corner. We are fighting a quiet war of hymns.
I prayed for the rain to stop and it snowed. {deity} has a sense of humor I do not share.
I forgot {deity}'s feast day. Now everything I touch breaks a little.

good.text: I told the story of the time I outran a carp. Everyone believed it. Even me.
We debated whether cats count as nobles. We agreed: worse.
The mayor asked for my opinion. He wrote nothing down, but he asked.
I made a new friend by complaining about the stairs. Shared suffering is the best mortar.

bad.text: I told my best joke and someone explained it back to me. Wrongly.
I was midway through a fine rant when the dinner bell rang. An unfinished rant festers.
A migrant corrected my pronunciation of 'magma'. In my own fortress!
I argued that plump helmets are mushrooms. They are. I lost anyway.

good.text: There is a cat figurine on my shelf. The only cat that has never knocked anything over.
A bard performed in the tavern. I did not understand the song. I clapped anyway.
I saw an engraving of the fortress founding. I am in it, in the background, hauling.
The new statue in the plaza shows a dwarf punching a tree. Finally, public art I support.

bad.text: The bard sang a song about elves. In our tavern. Over our ale.
Someone engraved the time I fell down the well. In great detail. With labels.
The mayor's statue is bigger than the founder's. Politics.
There is a poem about carp on the dining hall wall, and I have to eat beneath it.

good.text: I blocked a crossbow bolt with my mug. The mug survived. The ale did not.
I sparred with the captain and landed one punch. One! I am having it engraved.
The goblin ambush ran straight into our traps. I just stood there with my axe, looking heroic.
I kicked a troll in the shin. It sat down and wept. Very moving.

bad.text: My militia captain keeps scheduling training during dinner.
I swung at a goblin and hit the door frame. The door frame won.
The war dog fled before I did. That is a first, and I resent it.
I lost my helmet in battle and my dignity shortly after.

good.text: The ghost of the old miner still digs at night. Free labor. I am not complaining.
A friendly ghost reminded me where I left my pick. Very helpful dead people here.
I told the ghost a joke and it laughed. A cold laugh, but a laugh.
Since we engraved the slab, the halls are quiet. I miss the moaning a little.

bad.text: The ghost keeps arranging my socks into an unsettling pattern.
A ghost followed me to the latrine. There are limits.
The brewer's ghost haunts the stills. Now all the ale is cold. Too cold.
I woke at three in the morning with a ghost on my chest, asking about its slab.

good.text: The goats followed me across the pasture. I am their leader now.
A kitten fell asleep in my helmet. I will be going helmetless for a while.
I named the new alpaca after myself. We have the same haircut.
The war dog fetched me a goblin's boot. Thoughtful creature.

bad.text: A pig ate my lunch, then looked at me as if I were dessert.
The peacocks screech at dawn. Every dawn. All of them.
A cat adopted me without asking. Now I am responsible for a creature that despises me.
The cave crocodiles got out of their cage again. They wait by the stairs.

good.text: I sold the humans a stone mug for a whole bolt of silk. They have no idea what they did.
The caravan brought cheese from the mountainhomes. It tastes like my childhood, plus mold.
A merchant says our fortress is sung about in far-off lands. Probably lying. Still flattering.
The dwarven caravan brought gossip from home: my old rival lost his beard in a forge accident.

bad.text: The traders asked for wood. We are a stone fortress! Why would we have wood?
The broker fell asleep at the depot and the humans left with our patience.
I wanted to buy a new pick, and the merchant only had elven baskets.
The trade depot was built outside the walls. The goblins came to trade too, by force.

good.text: If you must know, {about} has me feeling {adj}. Print it in big letters.
I woke up thinking about {about}, and I was still {adj} about it at lunch.
Some dwarves get poems written about them. I get {about}, and I am {adj} about that.
Between you, me and the cat, {about} has left me feeling {adj}.

bad.text: Every time someone mentions {about}, I go {adj} all over again. Thanks for that.
{about}. Just {about}. If you were me, you would be {adj} too.
I carved my feelings about {about} into a rock. The rock says {adj}.
The overseer says I dwell on {about}. I do. It makes me {adj}, and then I dwell on that.

job.text: If your trade were a stone, which stone would it be?
Does your work ever get you out of hauling?
What tool could you not live without?
What is the hardest part of your trade that nobody notices?
How did you end up doing what you do in {fort}?
Would an elf understand your job if we explained it very slowly?

mood.text: Has anything thrown a mug at your spirits lately?
On a scale from raw plump helmet to masterwork, how are you?
How is your beard feeling, emotionally?
Would you say you are thriving, or merely not on fire?
How has {fort} been treating your nerves?

complaint.text: What would make you throw a tantrum this week?
Who is the worst hauler in {fort}, and why is it not you?
If you had a lever, what would you flood?
What is the one job you would ban forever?
What does the overseer keep getting wrong?
What drives you to the edge of a strange mood?

deity.text: Does your god have opinions on ale?
What do you ask of the gods, mostly?
Do the gods listen down here, under all this rock?
Has your faith ever saved you from a carp?
Do you have a favorite hymn?
Where in {fort} do you go to pray?

kin.text: What is the best thing about your {rel}?
Do you and {kin} share a trade, or just grudges?
What would {kin} say about you, if we asked?
Has your {rel} ever embarrassed you in the dining hall?
When did you last share a mug with {kin}?

nokin.text: Would you marry for a bigger bedroom?
What would your ideal companion be like?
Any family back in the mountainhomes?
Who keeps you company in the evenings?
Does a cat count as family?

last.text: Anything to tell the overseer, while the overseer is reading?
If you had one mug to raise, who would you toast?
What do you hope the next {season} brings?
What is the secret to a long life in {fort}?
How would you like to be remembered?
Any warnings for our younger readers?

job_match.text: I am {prof} through and through. {level} {skill}, with the scars to prove it, mostly from stairs.
Every fort needs a {level} {skill}. This one got me, and frankly it does not deserve me.
My grandmother was a {skill}. I am a {level} {skill}. Family tradition, with improvements.
I kept a tally on the wall of every job I finished as {level} {skill}. I ran out of wall.
When something breaks, they shout for the {prof}. When it is fixed, they forget. Such is life as a {level} {skill}.
I do not do it for glory. I do it because I am a {level} {skill} and nobody else will.

job_mismatch.text: They wrote {prof} on my door by mistake. I am a {level} {skill}, and I have stopped correcting them.
I came here to be the {prof}. The fortress had other plans: {level} {skill}.
Ask me to do {prof} work and I will stare at you. Ask the {level} {skill} and I will stare a bit less.
My trade is {prof}, but the overseer keeps handing me {skill} jobs. Now I am {level}. Funny how that works.
Officially {prof}. Unofficially {level} {skill}. Spiritually, still waiting for my bedroom.
I have the title of {prof} and the hands of a {level} {skill}. The two have never been introduced.

skill2_good.text: I am also a fine {skill2}. It is the hobby that pays in ale.
On rest days I am the {skill2}. A dwarf once named a child after my work. Just the one.
The {skill2} work? I could do it asleep. Once, I did.
Do not let the title fool you. My {skill2} work is the talk of the tavern.
Quietly, I am a gifted {skill2}. The quiet part is my modesty. It is very small.
My second trade is {skill2}. Some say it is really my first. I let them.

skill2_bad.text: I also attempt the {skill2} trade. 'Attempt' is the important word there.
My {skill2} work is best described as enthusiastic.
I once helped out as {skill2}. They still have not found all the pieces.
I am a {skill2} the way a goblin is a guest: technically, and nobody is happy about it.
Every apprentice {skill2} needs a first disaster. I have had eleven.
The {skill2} workshop has a drawing of my face on the door, crossed out.

mood_ecstatic.text: Ecstatic! I tipped my helmet to a goblin by mistake, and even that felt right.
I am happier than a miner who just struck adamantine. Not that I did. Not that I would tell you.
So joyful I offered to haul. Voluntarily. Mark the date.
Perfect. My bedroom, my ale, my beard: all magnificent. Next question.
Elated. Any lighter and I would float up into that terrible sky.
Wonderful! I have not had a single bad thought since the last caravan.

mood_happy.text: Good, thanks. My socks matched this morning. Both of them.
Pleasant. I found an extra plump helmet in my pocket. Old, but a nice surprise.
Rather well. The cat let me sit in my own chair.
Happy. Not cartwheel happy, but solid quiet-nod happy.
In good spirits, and in good ale, which helps the spirits.
Not bad at all. My last job finished without one cancellation notice.

mood_content.text: So-so. Like ale that has been left out. Still ale.
Even. Level. Like a well-smoothed floor.
Fine, in the sense that nothing has exploded today.
Content, mostly. I would like one more chair, but I am not greedy.
Neither up nor down. Somewhere around ground level, which is too close to the sky.
Adequate. I would rate myself well-crafted. Not finely. Just well.

mood_stressed.text: Twitchy. A door slammed and I dropped a whole tray of mugs.
On edge. I have been arguing with my pick, and losing.
Strained. My list of complaints just started a second page.
Frazzled. The overseer moves my workshop more often than I move my feet.
Uneasy. I sleep with one eye open now, mostly on the cats.
Stretched thin, like the last ale at the bottom of the barrel.

mood_very_stressed.text: Dreadful. I have started a grudge against the floor. The floor knows why.
Bad. I am one cancelled job away from screaming at a wheelbarrow.
Wretched. I asked for a hug and someone handed me a crutch.
Rotten. I cried into my stew, which honestly improved the seasoning.
Not good. I have counted every crack in the ceiling and named the worst ones.
Grim. My beard is full of knots, and I think they are emotional.

mood_breaking.text: Stand back. I can hear the furniture begging.
I am this close to going berserk, and I only tell you because you have a pen.
I am fine, I said, while holding a chair over my head.
Something is about to get thrown, and the mugs know it. They are trembling on the shelf.
Tell my family I said good luck. To the fortress, not to me.
Hear that? That is my last nerve being hauled off to a stockpile.

deity.text: {deity} and I have an arrangement. I pray, and {deity} pretends not to see me nap.
I wear a little carving of {deity} on a string. It has saved me from three cave-ins and one cook.
{deity} is the reason I still have both ears. Long story. Involves a troll.
I named my pick after {deity}. Every swing is a small prayer, and a small rock.
Some dwarves doubt the gods. I doubt the dwarves. {deity} is fine.
I once heard {deity} speak. It may have been the plumbing. I choose to believe.

kin_alive.text: {kin}, my {rel}? We eat breakfast together and argue about which of us is the better dwarf. Me.
My {rel} {kin} is the only one who can tell when I am lying. I avoid {kin} at dice.
{kin} taught me everything I know, except humility. That lesson did not take.
I made {kin} a mug once. {kin} still uses it, which is as close as a dwarf gets to saying I love you.
My {rel}, {kin}, works on the far side of the fort. We wave across the chasm every morning.
{kin}? Doing well. Recently started a feud with a goat, and is winning.

kin_dead.text: My {rel}, {kin}, rests below. Every time I pass the tomb, I knock twice. It was our joke.
{kin} left me a pick and a grudge. I use both daily.
We lost {kin} to a carp. I have not forgiven water since.
I carved {kin}'s name over my bedroom door. Now they watch over me, and my socks.
{kin} would have liked this fortress. Would have complained about it endlessly, but liked it.
I still set out {kin}'s favorite stool at dinner. Nobody sits on it. Nobody dares.

nokin.text: No kin. I am a lone dwarf, like one stone in a very large wall.
Family? I came here with six strangers and a wagon. We are not close.
Nobody yet. I am waiting for a dwarf who appreciates a good drainage channel.
No family, but the tavern keeper knows my name, which is nearly as good.
I had a sweetheart once. Then a migrant wave brought someone with a longer beard.
Single. The whole bed is mine, including the cold side.

signoff.text: Never build your stockpile next to the magma. Or do, and write the Herald a letter about it.
Dig in straight lines, and life will mostly follow.
Take a mug of ale to your neighbor. Then take it back. It is your ale.
If a dwarf in a strange mood asks for your sock, give it. Do not argue.
Wear a helmet in the caverns. Wear two near the stairs.
Say hello to the trader, goodbye to your bins, and never thank an elf.
Keep your pick sharp and your opinions sharper.
If the drawbridge is up, stay inside. If it is down, stay inside anyway.
Wash your beard before festivals. The mayor notices.
Never pull a lever you did not label yourself.
Lock up the cheese. The cats are organizing.
Always look up before you mine. Something might be looking down.
Give your haulers a break and your nobles a long hallway.
Be patient with migrants. You were one once, and you were terrible.
Rest your back, raise your mug, and lower your expectations.
Never trust a quiet cavern or a cheerful goblin.
Sweep your floors. Somewhere in that dust is someone's sock.
Hide your best chair when the noble comes calling.
Stay off the ice in spring. That is how you meet the carp.
Remember the fallen, honor the brewers, and forget the elves.
May your stone be smooth and your ale never warm.
Go to bed early. The siege will still be there in the morning.

decks.text: Mid-{job}, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, waved our reporter over and immediately regretted it.
The Herald caught {dwarf} ({age}, {prof}) halfway through '{job}' and asked for a few words. We got several.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, did not stop '{job}' for the Herald, but did slow down slightly, which counts.
Our correspondent shadowed {dwarf}, {age}, the {prof}, through one round of '{job}' and three complaints.
We found {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, busy with '{job}', and asked the questions nobody else in {fort} dares to.
Still dusty from '{job}', {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, gave the Herald an interview between sighs.
The Herald's {season} profile: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, currently and grudgingly on '{job}'.
{dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was mid-{job} when our reporter arrived holding ale. Negotiations were brief.
Readers asked who keeps {fort} running. Today's answer: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, doing '{job}'.
Leaning on the tools of '{job}', {dwarf}, {age}, the fort's {prof}, spoke to the Herald at length.
Between grunts of effort on '{job}', {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, shared some views on life in {fort}.
Our reporter tripped over {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, mid-{job}. The apology became an interview.
Ask the fort about '{job}' and they point to {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}. So the Herald went and asked.

idle_decks.text: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, was found lying in the meeting hall pondering the ceiling. The Herald pondered too.
No job, no hurry: {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, talked to the Herald while carefully not doing anything.
We caught {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, between tasks and between mugs, and asked about everything.
{dwarf}, {age}, the fort's {prof}, has no current assignment and a great many opinions.
Found leaning on a wall in {fort} this {season}, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, had nowhere to be. Until now.
The overseer forgot to give {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, any work. The Herald did not forget its questions.
Spotted idling by the still, {dwarf}, {age}, {prof}, swore it was a short break. We pulled up a stool.
